source_book: NCERT Class 12 Physics, Ch.7 Alternating Current, §7.9 Transformers — table-of-contents reference only; teaching authored from first principles, no sequence/example/figure imported. EIGHTH and LAST of 8 in the founder-reordered Ch.7 map (ac_voltage_resistor -> ac_voltage_inductor -> ac_voltage_capacitor -> phasors -> series_lcr_circuit -> ac_power_factor -> lc_oscillations -> transformer). This sim teaches the two-coil machine: one AC-driven flux circulating a closed iron core threads BOTH a primary and a secondary winding, inducing in each turn an equal share of EMF so that Vs/Vp = Ns/Np, while an ideal transformer passes power through unchanged (Vp*Ip = Vs*Is, so voltage up means current down); it works ONLY on CHANGING flux, never steady DC (the null-result PIVOT #2, STATE_3); real cores leak a little (copper heat, eddy currents fought by lamination, hysteresis, stray flux, STATE_8-9); and it thereby makes long-distance power transmission possible — step up to cut I^2R line loss, step down for safe use (STATE_7, cashing ac_power_factor's grid-transmission anchor seed). SCOPE: does not re-derive Faraday's law, rms values, real power, or I^2R heating (settled one-clause callbacks from the sealed siblings), does not quantify mutual inductance M in henries (Ch.6's inductance atomic), does not treat loaded-primary back-EMF regulation or magnetizing current (beyond syllabus; declared honest-unnarrated behaviour), and does not treat rectification or switch-mode electronics (out of scope). Conceptual-only (no mode_overrides), EPIC-L-first (no epic_c_branches; the two genuine transformer misconceptions -- 'step-up is free power' and 'a transformer works on DC too' -- are confronted inside EPIC-L via Rule 16a misconception_watch at exactly STATE_6 (PRIMARY) and STATE_3 (second pivot), each a straightforward wrong-consequence-first contrast beat, never a predict-pause). Routed to the NEW field_3d 'transformer' scenario (prefix tfr_) -- a Class-B clone-sibling of the sealed lc_oscillation scenario (inherits its chrome-family CSS geometry, battery+switch assembly inverted for an AC/DC source selector, bar-gauge pane, band/strip machinery) plus coil/source-ring assets from the element scenarios. The genuinely NEW machinery is the rectangular laminated core with circulating violet flux tubes, TWO electrically-disjoint windings (primary fixed at Np=100, secondary a live-growing Ns), the AC/DC source throw with its single blip then a steady DC dead-hold, the per-turn tick cascade, the scripted Ns turns ramp with thumb-lockstep, the lamp+four-meter instrument set, the Pp|Ps power-bar ledger with four named leak branches, the transmission strip (direct-send vs stepped-up phases), and the STATE_9 lamination zoom-lens cutaway (the concept's one true Rule-33 interior view). Zero edits to any sealed scenario (engine build tracked separately from this JSON authoring pass; renderer implementation is peter_parker:renderer_primitives scope, not json_author's -- the field_3d_config below IS the contract the engine dispatch builds against). Handoff FROM lc_oscillations: inherits the chapter's completed energy story ('an ideal element pair spends nothing; only real resistance/leaks spend') and the settled chapter apparatus conventions -- withholds mutual inductance, turns ratio, and voltage step-up/down entirely (this concept's own front door). CHAPTER END: transformer is concept 8 of 8 -- with this JSON, Ch.7 Alternating Current is COMPLETE. No further concept handoff; no DELIVERS/WITHHOLDS seed is emitted.

real_world_anchor.primary: The journey every watt makes to reach a wall socket. ac_power_factor seeded the grid-transmission story; this concept cashes it. Between any power station and any home stand transformers — the voltage is stepped UP to a very high value at the station (STATE_7's ×100 loss-collapse arithmetic is the entire reason), carried across country on transmission lines at a current too small to waste itself as wire heat, then stepped DOWN — stage by stage — finally to the mains voltage at the street, before it reaches a socket. Culture-neutral (no country, no named utility; 'the mains voltage' phrased neutrally, Rule 35b), the widest-syllabus-overlap device there is, and physics-true at depth.
real_world_anchor.secondary: The small warm brick that charges a phone works the same turns trick — at a much faster rhythm than the mains, by design — to step the wall's voltage down to the few volts a phone can drink. And the low hum audible near any large transformer is STATE_8's flexing core, made real. Nothing anchor-shaped is drawn (Rule 24; anchors live in narration); no regional constant is ever numeralized (35b).

N_p.name: Primary turn count — FIXED, never a slider (the reference winding)

N_s.name: Secondary turn count — the ONE live guided control in the whole concept (STATE_5 post-ramp only; STATE_11 all four sliders live)

V_p.name: Primary supply voltage — RMS (every meter in this sim reads rms). NEW declared work point (10.0 V rms), reconciled against the chapter's own vm=10 V peak and the siblings' 7.07 V rms work point — neither the peak nor the sibling rms value is rendered here.

f.name: Source frequency — the chapter's watchable flux rhythm; the real mains rate is phrased neutrally and never numeralized (35b)

R_load.name: Secondary load resistance — the lamp/resistive load

R_line.name: Transmission-line resistance — STATE_7 ONLY, narrative constant, never a slider; chosen so BOTH loss displays land exact at the declared 3dp precision. Numerically equals the chapter's retired series R — a different object (a transmission line), never juxtaposed.

omega.name: True angular frequency — feeds ONLY the Phi_m closed form, never on-screen degree display

omega_deg_per_s.name: Angular speed in deg/s — the degree-native rendering clock theta(t) (fleet dialect)

theta.name: Instantaneous phase, the state's OWN clock (Rule 26). theta0=0 at EVERY guided state's entry.
theta.derived: theta = omega_deg_per_s * t   [t = time since STATE ENTRY, pure closed form, zero accumulators]

T.name: Period of one full AC cycle at the active f (T=4.00s at defaults, the chapter rate)

per_turn.name: EMF per turn — the STATE_4 SUPPORTING result. Dual-labeled once 'volts per turn' at STATE_4, bare thereafter (38d). IDENTICAL on both windings at every ratio (verified: 0.100 V/turn at ratio 1 AND ratio 2).

Phi_m.name: Peak flux amplitude threading the closed core — depends ONLY on V_p, N_p, f; independent of N_s and R_load (the STATE_5 invariant, debuts STATE_1)

secondary_closed.name: Mechanical gate — a scene/apparatus pose flag, NOT a slider. 0 at STATE_1 ONLY (secondary mechanically open). 1 from STATE_2 onward, including STATE_3's DC dead-hold — the loop stays a rendered CLOSED path even while dead (Preamble B4: distinct from STATE_1's open pose).

V_s.name: Secondary voltage (rms), AC states only — THE transformer law, core-ring result debuted STATE_5. Gated to 0 by secondary_closed=0 at STATE_1; STATE_3's DC hold uses I_p_dc instead (never this formula).

I_s.name: Secondary current (rms), AC states only — set by the load alone

P_s.name: Secondary (load) power — what the secondary actually delivers

P_p.name: Primary power, IDEAL (no loss) — equals P_s exactly, the STATE_6 PRIMARY-aha quantity, used STATE_1-7/10/11. STATE_8 ALONE substitutes the separate REAL P_p_real — never conflate the two (Section 6 binding item 15).

I_p.name: Primary current (rms), IDEAL — set by power conservation, never independently chosen

v_p_t.name: Instantaneous primary voltage — the 0-phase reference (Preamble A). Continues even with the secondary open/dead (STATE_1/3) — the source keeps driving the primary loop regardless of the secondary's state.

Phi_t.name: Instantaneous flux, AC states — LAGS v_p_t by 90deg (Faraday, Preamble A). NOT active during STATE_3's DC hold (see flux_density_frac_dc) — never evaluate this formula during the dc_hold cue window.

v_s_t.name: Instantaneous secondary voltage — IN PHASE with v_p_t (ideal, same-sense convention, no leakage reactance, Preamble A)

i_s_t.name: Instantaneous secondary current — resistive load, in phase with v_s_t

i_p_t.name: Instantaneous primary current — by turns-ratio + power conservation, SAME phase as i_s_t

p_p_t.name: Instantaneous primary power — LITERAL pointwise product (32a caution), never an independently-animated curve that merely agrees

p_s_t.name: Instantaneous secondary power — LITERAL pointwise product

bead_frac_p_t.name: Primary-loop bead position — oscillates about home 0.5, phase-locked to i_p_t (fleet oscillating-bead convention)

bead_frac_s_t.name: Secondary-loop bead position — SAME theta, own amplitude scale, ZERO before STATE_2's closure and during STATE_3's DC dead-hold (secondary_closed / DC-null gates apply upstream via i_s_t)

A_frac_p.name: Primary bead-excursion visual scale, calibrated at defaults, clamped for explore extremes

A_frac_s.name: Secondary bead-excursion visual scale, calibrated at defaults, clamped for explore extremes

release_beat_deltaT.name: STATE_2 switch-closes-to-loop-wakes readable beat (32a cause-first gap)

throw_deltaT.name: STATE_3 blade-swing duration, AC pose to DC pose, before the blip fires

blip_deltaT.name: STATE_3 throw-instant transient bump duration (needle-kick + lamp-flash, Preamble B3 — no numeral)

turns_ramp_deltaT.name: STATE_5 scripted N_s ramp duration (100->200, thumb+label lockstep, F1 scar duty)

turn_count_t.name: STATE_4 running turn counter — closed form, 0..N_p

turn_bar_V_t.name: STATE_4 voltage bar fill — lockstep with the counter, reuses per_turn exactly (never a second independent computation)

N_s_ramp_t.name: STATE_5 scripted turns ramp — 100 to 200. N_s goes plain-live (drag-seize) at script end; thumb+label MUST move in lockstep with this exact value (F1 ghost_compare_cause_invisible_slider_frozen prevention).

R_p_dc_demo.name: STATE_3-ONLY narrative prop (Preamble B2) — a small primary-winding DC resistance chosen for a legible demo current. Explicitly NOT the quantity behind STATE_8's copper-loss figure — never render this symbol on canvas.

V_batt_dc.name: STATE_3 battery voltage — reuses the SAME dial numeral as V_p's default (the prop swap, not a new unexplained voltage)

I_p_dc.name: STATE_3 steady one-way primary DC current (Preamble B2, Ohm's-law callback) — 3.33 A, collision-checked against every other locked numeral in this concept

dc_bead_rate.name: STATE_3 uniform one-way bead advance rate — visual only, proportional in spirit to I_p_dc

bead_frac_p_dc_t.name: STATE_3 primary-loop bead position — advances UNIFORMLY in ONE direction (never oscillates), a closed form of the post-blip sub-clock t2. Distinct formula from every AC state's bead_frac_p_t (32b no-teleport discipline).
bead_frac_p_dc_t.derived: bead_frac_p_dc_t = frac(0.5 + dc_bead_rate*t2)   [frac(x)=x-floor(x); t2 = max(t1-blip_deltaT,0), t1 = time since the throw-complete instant]

blip_env_t.name: STATE_3 throw-instant transient bump — drives ONLY the needle-kick + lamp-flash pose (Preamble B3, no numeral rendered anywhere)

flux_density_frac_dc.name: STATE_3 flux-tube visual density during the DC hold — PINNED at full (1.0) once the blip completes (Preamble B1); breathing amplitude -> 0. NEVER driven by Phi_t during STATE_3.

I_line_direct.name: STATE_7 phase-A line current — direct send at the transformer's OWN secondary voltage (20.0 V at the ratio-2 work point), no further step-up

I_line_stepped.name: STATE_7 phase-B line current — a SEPARATE transmission-side step-up lifts the send voltage x10 (to 200 V) before the line

loss_ratio.name: STATE_7 chip — EXACT ONLY at the declared 3dp precision (2dp form 3.20/0.03=106 is FORBIDDEN)

i_line_t.name: STATE_7 instantaneous line current — SAME theta clock; amplitude = I_line_direct (phase A) or I_line_stepped (phase B); drives the line glow, never independently animated (32a)
i_line_t.derived: i_line_t = sqrt(2)*I_line_phase*sin(radians(theta))   [I_line_phase = I_line_direct in phase A, I_line_stepped in phase B]

line_glow_t.name: STATE_7 line-glow drive — the honest heat proxy, averages to the exact loss_direct/loss_stepped values over a full cycle

copper_loss.name: STATE_8 declared pedagogical constant, valid ONLY at the ratio-2 work point (N_s=200,V_p=10.0,f=0.25,R_load=25.0). AUTHORED, not derived (no per-mechanism resistive model built in this concept).

eddy_loss.name: STATE_8 declared constant (STATE_9 opens this one qualitatively)

stray_loss.name: STATE_8 declared constant (breaks STATE_4's 'ALL flux threads EVERY turn' ideal promise — retro-link)

P_p_real.name: STATE_8 ONLY — the REAL primary draw. Never conflate with the ideal P_p used everywhere else (Section 6 binding item 15).
P_p_real.derived: P_p_real = P_s + copper_loss + eddy_loss + hysteresis_loss + stray_loss

eta.name: STATE_8 efficiency — displayed as integer percent (eta*100)

formulas.faraday_shared_flux: v_p(t) = N_p*dPhi/dt (STATE_1 mechanism, STATE_10 derivation link 1) -- Phi(t)=-Phi_m*cos(theta) is the unique closed form consistent with v_p(t)=sqrt(2)*V_p*sin(theta) (verified, Preamble A)
formulas.turns_ratio_law: V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p (STATE_5 core-ring result, measured before it is derived)
formulas.power_conservation_law: V_p*I_p = V_s*I_s exactly, ideal (STATE_6 PRIMARY aha) -- nothing amplified, volts traded for amps
formulas.dc_null_result: Under steady DC, dPhi/dt=0 -> induced EMF=0 in every turn regardless of flux magnitude (STATE_3 PIVOT #2) -- the throw itself was the last CHANGE this loop ever saw
formulas.per_turn_share: per_turn = V_p/N_p = V_s/N_s identically at every ratio (STATE_4 SUPPORTING result, verified: both equal 0.100 V/turn at ratio 1 AND ratio 2)
formulas.transmission_loss_law: P_loss = I^2*R_line, I=P/V -- stepping V up by k drops I by k and P_loss by k^2 (STATE_7, the grid's entire reason)
formulas.efficiency_law: eta = P_s/P_p_real = P_s/(P_s + sum of leaks) (STATE_8, real-device digression, extended ring only)
formulas.derivation_chain: eps_p=-N_p*dPhi/dt, eps_s=-N_s*dPhi/dt (SAME Phi) -> eps_s/eps_p=N_s/N_p -> V_s/V_p=N_s/N_p -> V_p*I_p=V_s*I_s -> I_p/I_s=N_s/N_p (STATE_10)

constraints: V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p at every instant -- the ideal transformer law (STATE_5).
V_p*I_p = V_s*I_s exactly under the ideal (no-loss) model used STATE_1-7/10/11 -- power passes through unchanged (STATE_6). Only STATE_8's separate P_p_real substitutes real leaks.
Phi_m = sqrt(2)*V_p/(N_p*omega) depends on V_p, N_p, f ALONE -- never on N_s or R_load (the STATE_5 invariant, verified unchanged across the entire N_s ramp).

A transformer transfers power ONLY via CHANGING flux -- steady DC sustains flux but induces zero secondary EMF (dPhi/dt=0 -> eps=0), regardless of how large or how long-sustained that flux is (STATE_3).
Real transformers always have P_p_real > P_s (eta<1) from copper/eddy/hysteresis/stray losses -- eta is bounded in (0,1), never negative, never exceeding 1 (STATE_8).
per_turn = V_p/N_p = V_s/N_s identically, on EITHER winding, at EVERY turns ratio -- verified 0.100 V/turn at both ratio 1 and ratio 2 (STATE_4).

aha_moment.statement: A transformer trades volts for amps — it never supplies free power.

STATE_1.title: One flux, driven by the primary, threads both windings — the secondary sits open and dark

scene_composition.text: No wire joins them — only the flux does

tts_sentences.text_en: Two coils sit on one closed iron core, touching nothing.
The primary carries an alternating current, and the changing flux it makes circulates through the whole core — threading both windings equally.
Right now the secondary's switch is open: no current flows there, no matter how strong the flux.

STATE_2.title: SUPPORTING aha — a closed loop linked to a changing flux carries current, with no wires

scene_composition.text: A changing flux through a loop drives an EMF

tts_sentences.text_en: Close the secondary's own switch — and current flows, with no wire back to the source.
A changing flux through a loop drives an EMF: the same law that kicked a needle in the induction chapter.
The lamp lights; the meters agree — ten volts, point four amps, on both sides.

STATE_3.title: PIVOT #2 — a transformer needs CHANGING flux; steady DC, however large, transfers nothing

scene_composition.text: Only CHANGE crosses — that's why the grid is AC

tts_sentences.text_en: Swap in a steady battery.
At the throw, one blip — then the secondary stops.
The primary still carries current, sustaining a huge, frozen flux — current flowing, flux present, nothing changing.
So the secondary gets nothing.
Only changing flux crosses; that is why the grid runs on AC.

misconception_watch.belief: A transformer works on DC too — steady current still makes flux.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: The DC throw gives ONE blip (secondary needles kick, lamp flashes — the change itself), then the primary keeps a steady one-way current flowing (Iₚ steady nonzero, beads streaming) sustaining flux tubes frozen at FULL density — while Iₛ = Vₛ = 0.00 and the lamp is dark: current still flowing, flux still there, nothing crossing.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: The current is still flowing and the flux is still there — but nothing CHANGES, so the secondary gets nothing; only change crosses, and that is why transformers, and the grid, live on AC.

STATE_4.title: Every turn shares the same flux and gains the same equal share

scene_composition.text: Every turn drinks the same equal share

tts_sentences.text_en: Every turn shares the same changing flux, so every turn gains the same tenth of a volt.
Watch a hundred turns light one by one — a running counter, a bar filling to ten volts, in lockstep.
The secondary's own hundred turns share that same flux — which is why it also reads ten volts.

STATE_5.title: Crank the turns and watch the voltage obey: Vₛ/Vₚ = Nₛ/Nₚ

scene_composition.text: More turns than the primary — a step-up transformer

tts_sentences.text_en: Watch the secondary gain turns — a hundred climbing to two hundred, live.
The voltage climbs with it: ten volts to twenty.
The flux never changed — only how many turns share it.
More turns than the primary makes a step-up transformer; wind fewer, and it steps down.

STATE_6.title: PRIMARY aha — nothing is amplified: VₚIₚ = VₛIₛ, volts up means amps down

scene_composition.text: A trade, not a gift — nothing is amplified

tts_sentences.text_en: Twenty volts looks like a gain — but watch the current: point eight amps, half of the primary's one point six.
Sixteen watts goes in; sixteen watts comes out — no more, no less.
A transformer trades volts for amps; it never supplies free power.

misconception_watch.belief: Step-up = free power: if the voltage doubled, the secondary delivers more than the primary draws.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: The dimmed ghost chip 'step-up = free power?' latched beside the four live meters — struck as Iₚ = 1.60 A visibly DOUBLES Iₛ = 0.80 A and the Pₚ|Pₛ bars sit dead level at 16.0 W; chip 10.0 × 1.60 = 20.0 × 0.80 = 16.0 W.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: A transformer trades volts for amps — every watt the secondary delivers, the primary drew; nothing is amplified.

STATE_7.title: Step up, lose less — the line runs a hundred times cooler

tts_sentences.text_en: Send sixteen watts down a line directly at twenty volts: point eight amps, and the wire burns three point two watts as heat — a fifth of everything.
Step it up tenfold to two hundred volts first: point zero eight amps, and the loss collapses to point zero three two watts — a hundredth.

STATE_8.title: Real transformers leak: copper heat, eddy currents, hysteresis, stray flux — η = 95%

tts_sentences.text_en: Real transformers leak.
The primary now draws sixteen point eight watts, but only sixteen reach the secondary.
Copper heat, eddy currents, a magnet-flipping hysteresis cost, and stray flux each take a small share — ninety-five percent efficient.
That faint hum near a big transformer is the core itself flexing.

STATE_9.title: Inside the core: solid metal forms wide eddy whirlpools; lamination stops them

scene_composition.text: Every real core you'll ever see is laminated

tts_sentences.text_en: Inside a solid core, the changing flux drives wide eddy whirlpools — wasted heat, going nowhere.
Slice the same metal into thin, insulated layers, and the whirlpools shrink to slivers; the heat collapses.
That is why every real transformer core you will ever see is laminated.

STATE_10.title: Derivation: the same dΦ/dt in every turn gives the ratio and the current law

tts_sentences.text_en: Both coils sit on the same flux, so εₚ equals minus Nₚ dΦ by dt, and εₛ equals minus Nₛ dΦ by dt.
Divide: εₛ over εₚ equals Nₛ over Nₚ.
With no losses, power passes through unchanged, so Iₚ over Iₛ equals Nₛ over Nₚ — twenty volts, point eight amps, as measured.

STATE_11.title: Explore — the transformer under the teacher's hands

tts_sentences.text_en: Try the controls — drag the turns, the voltage, the frequency, and the load, and watch the ratio, the currents, and the lamp respond live.

assessment.mastery_definition: A student has mastered the transformer when they can (1) explain that a changing flux threading a shared closed core links two electrically-disjoint windings, so energy crosses with no wire between them (Faraday's law, no direct conduction); (2) apply the ideal turns-ratio law Vs/Vp = Ns/Np to identify step-up vs step-down and compute the secondary voltage; (3) explain ideal power conservation Vp*Ip = Vs*Is — a transformer trades volts for amps, never amplifying power, and a real transformer draws slightly MORE than the ideal value due to internal losses; (4) explain that a transformer requires CHANGING flux — steady DC sustains a flux but induces zero secondary EMF, producing only a single transient blip at switch-on; (5) explain why real cores are laminated — thin insulated sheets chop the wide eddy-current loops that would otherwise waste energy as heat in a solid core; and (6) explain why long-distance transmission runs at high voltage — stepping up voltage lowers the line current (I=P/V), and since line loss is I²R, the loss collapses by the square of the voltage ratio.

questions.stem: A primary coil carries alternating current, and a secondary coil sits on the same closed iron core with no wire joining the two circuits. How does energy reach the secondary coil?

options.A: The primary's changing magnetic flux threads the secondary through the shared core and induces an EMF there — Faraday's law, with no direct electrical contact at all
options.B: Free electrons conduct directly through the solid iron core from the primary winding into the secondary winding
options.C: The two coils are close enough that static charge simply jumps the air gap between them
options.D: Sound vibrations from the primary coil physically shake the secondary coil's charges into motion

distractor_misconceptions.B: This is the confronted misconception — the two loop meshes are electrically disjoint; no electron ever crosses from one winding to the other. Only the changing flux threading the shared core links them, not conduction.
distractor_misconceptions.C: There is no electrostatic jump between the windings — this is an electromagnetic induction effect through the shared changing flux, not a static-discharge phenomenon.
distractor_misconceptions.D: Sound has no role here — the coupling is purely electromagnetic, through the changing magnetic flux linking both windings via the shared core.

questions.tested_idea: Two magnetically-coupled but electrically-disjoint circuits transfer energy via a shared changing flux (Faraday's law), never by direct conduction.
questions.parallel_form_stem: If a thick copper bar bridged the primary and secondary windings, would that be what actually carries the current across in a transformer?

questions.stem: A transformer has Nₚ = 100 turns on the primary and Nₛ = 200 turns on the secondary, running from a 10.0 V rms AC supply. Is this step-up or step-down, and what is the secondary voltage?

options.A: Step-up transformer (more secondary turns); Vₛ = Vₚ×(Nₛ/Nₚ) = 10.0×(200/100) = 20.0 V
options.B: The voltage stays 10.0 V no matter the turns — voltage can't change without a direct wire connection between the windings
options.C: Step-down transformer, since twice as many turns means the voltage is halved to 5.0 V
options.D: The turns ratio only matters for current, not voltage — Vₛ is undefined without knowing the resistances

distractor_misconceptions.B: This is the confronted misconception — voltage transforms perfectly well with no direct wire at all; the shared changing flux does the job. More secondary turns means more induced EMF, not zero.
distractor_misconceptions.C: More secondary turns than primary turns makes it step-UP, not step-down — the ratio direction is flipped here. Twice the turns gives twice the voltage, not half.
distractor_misconceptions.D: The turns ratio sets the VOLTAGE ratio directly (Vₛ/Vₚ = Nₛ/Nₚ), independent of load resistance — resistance only affects how much current the secondary draws once Vₛ is fixed.

questions.tested_idea: The ideal transformer voltage law Vₛ/Vₚ = Nₛ/Nₚ: more secondary turns steps voltage up, fewer steps it down.
questions.parallel_form_stem: The same transformer instead has Nₛ = 50 turns — is it now step-up or step-down, and what is Vₛ?

questions.stem: An ideal transformer's secondary delivers 16.0 W to its load. How much power does the primary draw from the supply?

options.A: 16.0 W exactly (ideal, no losses) — a little more than 16.0 W in a real transformer, due to small internal leaks
options.B: 8.0 W — the transformer must be losing half the power somewhere, since the current dropped
options.C: 32.0 W — a step-up transformer doubles the power along with the voltage
options.D: It cannot be determined without knowing the exact resistances of both windings

distractor_misconceptions.B: This is the confronted misconception's mirror — a smaller secondary current does NOT mean less power arrived; power conservation, VₚIₚ = VₛIₛ, holds exactly in the ideal case. The primary draws the full 16.0 W, not half.
distractor_misconceptions.C: This is the PRIMARY confronted misconception — a transformer trades volts for amps; it never multiplies power. Doubling voltage halves current, and the product (power) stays fixed at 16.0 W ideal.
distractor_misconceptions.D: Power conservation alone (VₚIₚ = VₛIₛ) fixes the ideal primary power at exactly the secondary's 16.0 W — no winding resistance value is needed for the ideal case.

questions.tested_idea: Ideal power conservation across a transformer: VₚIₚ = VₛIₛ exactly — nothing is amplified, and real transformers draw slightly MORE than the ideal value due to internal losses.
questions.parallel_form_stem: If the secondary instead delivers 4.0 W to its load, how much power does an ideal primary draw?

questions.stem: The same transformer's primary is connected to a steady 10 V battery instead of the AC supply. What happens, and why?

options.A: One brief blip at the moment of connection, then nothing — a steady flux, however large, induces zero EMF in the secondary because the flux is no longer CHANGING
options.B: The transformer works exactly the same on DC as on AC, just with a steady output voltage
options.C: Nothing happens at all, not even a blip, because DC current can never create any magnetic flux
options.D: The secondary catches fire because the DC current is far more dangerous than AC in a transformer

distractor_misconceptions.B: This is the confronted misconception — a transformer needs CHANGING flux to induce anything; a steady DC current sustains a steady flux, but induces exactly zero EMF in the secondary once settled.
distractor_misconceptions.C: A steady DC current absolutely does create a magnetic flux (Ampere's/Biot-Savart physics) — the flux is real and large; it is only the CHANGE in flux that induces an EMF, and a steady flux has none.
distractor_misconceptions.D: This overstates the effect with no physical basis here — the concept's actual point is a quiet, instructive null result (secondary reads zero), not a dramatic failure.

questions.tested_idea: A transformer requires CHANGING flux — steady DC sustains flux but induces zero secondary EMF (dΦ/dt = 0), regardless of the flux's size.
questions.parallel_form_stem: Why does the secondary needle kick once at the exact instant the switch is thrown, but never again afterward?

questions.stem: Why is a real transformer's iron core built as a stack of thin, insulated laminations rather than one solid block of iron?

options.A: Thin insulated laminations chop the wide eddy-current whirlpools that would otherwise form in a solid core, cutting the wasted heat they cause
options.B: Laminating the core increases the magnetic flux it can carry, boosting the voltage produced
options.C: It is purely a manufacturing convenience — laminated sheets are cheaper to produce than a solid block
options.D: Laminations are needed so the primary and secondary windings don't touch each other

distractor_misconceptions.B: Lamination doesn't increase the flux the core carries — Φₘ is set by the supply voltage, turns, and frequency alone; lamination only reduces a specific real-device LOSS (eddy currents), not the ideal flux.
distractor_misconceptions.C: This isn't primarily a cost/manufacturing choice — it's a genuine physics fix: chopping the conducting loops available to eddy currents, which drains real energy as heat in a solid core.
distractor_misconceptions.D: Winding separation has nothing to do with core lamination — the primary and secondary never touch regardless of whether the core is solid or laminated; lamination is entirely about suppressing eddy currents.

questions.tested_idea: Laminating the core breaks up the wide conducting loops available to eddy currents, cutting a real (non-ideal) energy loss without changing the ideal flux.
questions.parallel_form_stem: If a transformer core were doubled in thickness but kept solid (not laminated), would the eddy-current heating go up or down?

questions.stem: The same 16.0 W is sent down a 5.0 Ω transmission line, once directly at 20 V and once after being stepped up tenfold to 200 V. Why does the high-voltage line lose far less power as heat?

options.A: Stepping up the voltage tenfold drops the line current tenfold; since line loss is I²R, the loss falls by a factor of 100
options.B: Higher voltage makes the current travel faster down the line, so it spends less time being resistively heated
options.C: The transmission line itself has less resistance when carrying a higher voltage
options.D: Power and voltage are unrelated to line loss — the loss depends only on the fixed line resistance, which never changes

distractor_misconceptions.B: Signal speed on a wire is not the relevant mechanism here — the loss is I²R, purely a function of the CURRENT magnitude and the fixed line resistance, not how 'fast' charge moves.
distractor_misconceptions.C: The line's resistance R_line = 5.0 Ω is a fixed property of the wire — it does not change with the voltage or current flowing through it.
distractor_misconceptions.D: Line loss depends directly on the current squared (P_loss = I²R_line) — since I = P/V, raising V for the same power P lowers I, and therefore lowers the loss, even with a fixed R_line.

questions.tested_idea: Transmission-line loss scales as I²R; stepping up the send voltage lowers the current (I = P/V) and collapses the I²R loss by the square of the voltage ratio.
questions.parallel_form_stem: If the send voltage were stepped up by a factor of 5 instead of 10, by what factor would the line loss fall?

engine_contract.phase_convention: ONE state-local theta(t) clock; v_p_t, v_s_t, i_s_t, i_p_t are ALL sin(theta) -- in phase, no leakage reactance modeled; Phi_t alone is -cos(theta), 90deg behind (Faraday's law itself, Preamble A). NEVER introduce a phi/lag variable anywhere in this concept.
engine_contract.radians_wrap: Every sin/cos call wraps its degree-native angle in radians(...) -- theta in every AC formula; blip_env_t's PI*clamp(...) argument is already radian-native, no wrap needed there.
engine_contract.s3_flux_hide: STATE_3 renders NO Phi numeral, ever -- only the qualitative badge 'dPhi/dt = 0'. flux_density_frac_dc=1.0 (constant) drives tube opacity/thickness during the DC hold. Phi_t (AC-only formula) must NOT be evaluated during STATE_3's dc_hold cue window (Preamble B1).
engine_contract.s3_blip_no_numeral: blip_env_t drives ONLY the needle-kick pose and lamp-flash brightness -- no HUD/chip numeral is ever attached to it (Preamble B3). Do not invent one.
engine_contract.s3_two_zeros: STATE_1's dark secondary (secondary_closed=0, mechanically open) and STATE_3's dead secondary (secondary_closed=1, zero EMF) MUST render visibly differently -- STATE_3's loop stays rendered CLOSED throughout (Preamble B4, binding on the engine AND eye-walker).
engine_contract.s8_declared_leak_constants: copper_loss/eddy_loss/hysteresis_loss/stray_loss are hand-authored 1dp constants valid ONLY at the ratio-2 work point (N_s=200,V_p=10.0,f=0.25,R_load=25.0) -- never wire them to a general formula that would also fire in STATE_11 explore (explore excludes leak bars entirely, ring gate 38b).
engine_contract.glow_pane_multiplier: STATE_6 and STATE_8's 'gauges' glow_focal must brighten the WHOLE gauge pane as a multiplier on its own live channel -- never per-bar (a Pp/Ps pair, or the leak ledger, must never visually imply one side 'matters more'). See glow_pane_multiplier:true on those two states.
engine_contract.subscript_compose: Pinned ASCII tokens V_p/V_s/I_p/I_s/N_p/N_s/P_p/P_s/Phi/eta compose-sweep to Vₚ Vₛ Iₚ Iₛ Nₚ Nₛ Pₚ Pₛ Φ η on ALL THREE text paths (DOM HUD innerHTML, canvas ctx.fillText, sprite labels). R_line stays literal (no subscript compose). Verify the compose regex handles LETTER subscripts (U+209A/U+209B) -- a NEW surface for the fleet (previously only digit/other-letter subscripts existed).
engine_contract.near_zero_clamp: |v_p_t|, |v_s_t|, |i_s_t|, |i_p_t|, |Phi_t| < half-LSB render unsigned 0.00 (crosses zero every cycle in every AC state).
engine_contract.s5_thumb_lockstep: During the scripted N_s ramp (STATE_5, ns_ramp_start_at_ms..+ns_ramp_dur_ms), the DOM slider thumb position + numeric label MUST move in lockstep with N_s_ramp_t -- never just the underlying physics/visual while the thumb sits frozen (F1 ghost_compare_cause_invisible_slider_frozen prevention).
engine_contract.s7_precision_exception: Loss values render at 3dp ONLY in STATE_7 (line_loss_precision_dp:3) -- nowhere else in the concept needs 3dp precision; do not propagate this exception to other states' I/P displays.
engine_contract.explorer_objects: tfr_switch (AC/DC source selector, Rule-27 stable ID, position 'A'|'B') is SCRIPTED-ONLY at STATE_3 -- do NOT add it as an explore-draggable object in STATE_11. The secondary switch closes ONCE at STATE_2 (scripted one-shot) and stays closed STATE_3-STATE_11 (secondary_closed=1) -- never re-opened, never independently draggable.
engine_contract.p_p_vs_p_p_real: P_p (ideal, = P_s) is used STATE_1-7/10/11; P_p_real (= P_s + leaks) is used ONLY at STATE_8. Keep them as two distinct physics_engine_config variables (already separate above) -- a single shared variable would silently break either STATE_6's 'nothing amplified' equality or STATE_8's '0.8W gap'.
engine_contract.no_bridge_invariant: The two loop meshes (primary, secondary) are electrically disjoint at every state -- no bead ever crosses between loops, no conductive path intersects both. Probe this at every state.
engine_contract.settled_pin_discipline: Every guided state's settled/frozen pose is PHASE-pinned (a v-extremum, the dead-hold, the cool phase, the laminated half) -- never a recurring instantaneous zero-crossing. No state freezes the master clock mid-guided; STATE_10 dims via E4 restore (reveal_hold), STATE_11 free-runs forever (Rule 37).

STATE_1.label: One AC-driven flux circulates the closed core and threads BOTH windings — the secondary sits open and dark
STATE_1.caption: One flux, two coils

STATE_2.label: SUPPORTING aha — close the secondary's own loop: current flows and the lamp lights, with NO wire to the source
STATE_2.caption: No wires — power crosses

STATE_3.label: PIVOT #2 — swap in a DC battery: one blip at the throw, then a large STEADY flux transfers nothing
STATE_3.caption: Steady flux — nothing crosses

STATE_4.label: Each turn shares the same changing flux, so every turn contributes the SAME 0.100 V; turns in series stack
STATE_4.caption: Every turn, equal share

STATE_5.label: Crank Nₛ 100→200 and Vₛ obeys: Vₛ/Vₚ = Nₛ/Nₚ (step-up; fewer turns = step-down)
STATE_5.caption: Turns set the voltage

STATE_6.label: PRIMARY aha — the volts doubled but the amps halved: VₚIₚ = VₛIₛ, the watts pass through untouched
STATE_6.caption: Volts up, amps down

STATE_7.label: Step up → tiny current → the line loss collapses ×100; step down at the house — why the grid exists
STATE_7.caption: Step up, lose less

STATE_8.label: Real transformers leak a little: four named losses; η = Pₛ/Pₚ ≈ 95%
STATE_8.caption: Real transformers leak

STATE_9.label: Inside the core: solid metal forms wide eddy whirlpools; lamination chops them — the leak stopped
STATE_9.caption: Thin slices stop eddies

STATE_10.label: Derivation: ε = −N·dΦ/dt on the SAME Φ → εₛ/εₚ = Nₛ/Nₚ; ideal power → Iₚ/Iₛ = Nₛ/Nₚ
STATE_10.caption: The ratio, derived

transformer.formula_text: εₚ = −Nₚ·dΦ/dt → εₛ = −Nₛ·dΦ/dt → εₛ/εₚ = Nₛ/Nₚ → Vₛ/Vₚ = Nₛ/Nₚ → Iₚ/Iₛ = Nₛ/Nₚ
